## Verdict
REVISE — Native observation and durable visible results are feasible, but safe automatic activation, consumption acknowledgement and command-scoped cancellation remain unproven.

## Critical gaps
- **Activation-time gating:** Pi’s queued `followUp` messages bypass `before_agent_start`, and the inspected API provides no per-message retraction. Queue-time affinity checks cannot prevent stale activation. Keep actionable completions in an extension-owned queue until a demonstrated gating boundary; otherwise disable automatic follow-up.
- **Acknowledgement:** `sendMessage` returns `void`; transcript insertion and `message_end` do not prove model consumption. Define separate persisted/displayed, activation-attempted and explicitly acknowledged states. Notification retries must not automatically retry agent work after an uncertain crash.
- **Cancellation scope:** No supplied evidence establishes an atomic “interrupt only this command sequence” operation. Checking identity and subsequently sending Ctrl+C can interrupt a replacement command. Defer job-scoped cancellation unless guarded native cancellation exists; an explicitly authorized pane interrupt is a different contract.

## Important improvements
- Make launch attribution a capability boundary. Per-pane extension serialization does not fence humans or other Pi processes; a baseline’s next completion is not necessarily this job. Require positively correlated evidence, otherwise retain unknown and quarantine further managed submissions pending reconciliation. Guaranteed shared-pane attribution may require daemon changes.
- Preserve aborted-execution rethrow behavior and publish detached-wait status through independent UI. Render the evidenced state—not unconditional “Still running,” which is false for launch-unknown or already-completed jobs.
